    The Code Interview

    An interviewer gives you a problem and a time limit, and watches. You must choose the right data structure, write working code, and justify it in terms of time and memory. Most developers never practiced that out loud.

    A field manual for busy Java developers: 48 real interview questions, each solved from brute force to optimal.

    Software Design Principles

    Stop writing code that works today—and breaks tomorrow.

    Software Design Principles: A Practical Guide to Building Software That Can Change gives working developers a clear, practical path from messy code to systems that are easy to understand, test, and evolve. Instead of treating principles as abstract rules, this book shows you when each one helps, what it costs, and when it can actually make your code worse.
